reader.requirement: For a format 1 INSPECT (and the tallying half of a format 3), when identifier-1, identifier-3 (pattern) or identifier-4 (BEFORE/AFTER delimiter) shares storage with a counter identifier-2, even through the same entry, the result is undefined at 85. The compiler owes no particular result, only acceptance of the legal source and a run that completes; any deterministic result conforms.

reader.edition-search: The overlap mechanism itself (InspectEmitter#CounterMayChangeInputs, #CounterMayOverlapTarget, #MayReadStorageOf, StorageOverlap#MayShareStorage, CobolInspect Tally/Replace/Convert) has no edition reference: grep 'Edition|CobolVersion|Std|Dialect|IsAtLeast|Version' over InspectEmitter.cs, CobolInspect.cs and StorageOverlap.cs found only a doc-comment mention of DialectBehavior in CobolInspect.cs; the edition consults are the binder's, listed.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes, only inside the undefined case: a format 3 whose counter is the DEPENDING ON object of an occurs-depending identifier-1 re-reads the length for the REPLACING half at 85 (O2=[9BBBBBBAAA] at 85, [9BBBAAAAAA] at 2023), following the two-statement reading of §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR17. The overlap mechanism (re-read after each counter store, docs/CONFORMANCE.md D-INS1/D-INS2) is the same at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover group/elementary overlap, a same-entry counter, pattern and BEFORE overlap, reference modification and a REDEFINES. They do not exercise an occurs-depending identifier-1 whose counter is the DEPENDING ON object, a signed counter that is identifier-1, a subscripted counter whose subscript is another counter, or an ODO group at count 0 (probed below).

reader.notes: GR13 leaves an overlapped counter undefined, so the rule asks only that legal source compile and run. It does at 85 for every overlap form probed, with the deterministic re-read choice documented as D-INS1/D-INS2 and shared with 2023. The one 85-specific divergence (format 3 ODO length re-read) is the GR17 arm and lies inside the undefined case.
